Setup Reference Row(s) for Forest Plots

setupDfRefRow.Rd

Generates the reference data frame (dfRefRow) required by getForestDF functions. It computes the baseline reference values and maps them onto the structure of the provided dfCovs.

Usage

setupDfRefRow(
  dfCovs,
  data,
  covariates,
  conditionalCovs = NULL,
  singleRef = TRUE,
  contRef = "median",
  catRef = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  refLevels = NULL,
  minLevels = 10,
  idVar = "ID",
  missVal = -99,
  nsig = 3,
  sep = "_"
)

Arguments

dfCovs

The covariate data frame generated by setupDfCovs().

data

The raw data frame used to calculate the reference values. Only the first record per subject (identified by idVar) is used.

covariates

A character vector of primary covariate base names - the covariates a reference should be computed from the data for. Base names, not encoded column names: GENO rather than GENO_2, GENO_3, GENO_4. It need not cover every column of dfCovs. A dfCovs column with no reference resolved for it is set to missVal, which a parameter function reads as "not active here" and answers with its own reference - so leaving a covariate out means use the model's reference for this one. A message names any columns this applies to.

conditionalCovs

A character vector of supplementary covariate base names. Defaults to NULL.

singleRef

Logical. If TRUE (default), returns a single-row data frame with every covariate at its reference value. If FALSE, returns a data frame with the dimensions of dfCovs, preserving missVal states while replacing active states with reference values.

contRef

Reference setting for continuous covariates: a number, "mean", "median" (default) or "model", or a named list of those with an optional default component.

catRef

Reference setting for categorical covariates: a level, "mode" (default), "lowest" or "model", or a named list of those with an optional default component. Replaces refLevels. When dfCovs came from setupDfCovs() this defaults to the catRef that call used, so it does not normally need repeating; supplying it here overrides that.

model

The NONMEM control stream, required when any reference is set to "model". Either a path to the .mod file or the list returned by createParamFunction().

refLevels

Deprecated. Use catRef.

minLevels

The maximum number of unique values a covariate can have to be treated as categorical. Default is 10.

idVar

The name of the subject identifier column. Defaults to "ID".

missVal

The numeric value indicating missing data in dfCovs. Defaults to -99.

nsig

The number of significant digits used when rounding a computed mean or median. An explicitly supplied value is never rounded. Defaults to 3.

sep

The separator between the covariate name and the level in the one-hot column names. When dfCovs came from setupDfCovs() this defaults to the separator that call used, so it does not normally need repeating; otherwise "_". Supplying it here overrides the recorded value.

Value

A data frame formatted to be passed as the dfRefRow argument.

Details

Choosing the reference. contRef and catRef both accept either a single setting applied to every covariate, or a named list with an entry per covariate plus an optional default component:

  • continuous - a number, "mean", "median" (default) or "model";

  • categorical - a level, "mode" (default), "lowest" or "model".

For example contRef = list(WT = 75, AGE = "mean", default = "median").

"model" and why it usually matters. A parameter function derived from the control stream falls back to the model's own reference whenever a covariate is inactive - the normalisation constant in (WT/75), or the branch PsN's scm marks ; Most common. If the reference row instead uses a statistic of the data, the two disagree and every row where that covariate is inactive is displaced from 1. Setting contRef = "model" and catRef = "model", with model pointing at the control stream (or at the list returned by createParamFunction()), removes that mismatch by construction. Statistics are otherwise computed on deduplicated baseline data, one record per idVar, matching setupDfCovs().

Categorical covariates. An explicit catRef level is both the reference subject's level and, for a multi-level covariate, the level dropped when one-hot encoding - so pass the same catRef here as to setupDfCovs(). Left unset, the reference subject takes the most common level while the encoding drops the lowest, which is the behaviour of earlier versions.

See also

setupDfCovs(), createParamFunction() vignette("Part3-deep-dive-forest-plot-inputs", package = "PMXForest") for how this fits the whole workflow.

Examples

dfData <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "SimVal/DAT-1-MI-PMX-2.csv", package = "PMXForest")
)
covs <- c("WT", "AGE", "SEX", "GENO")
dfCovs <- setupDfCovs(dfData, covariates = covs, idVar = "ID")

# Single-row reference: every covariate at its mode / median
setupDfRefRow(dfCovs, data = dfData, covariates = covs, idVar = "ID")
#>     WT AGE SEX GENO_2 GENO_3 GENO_4 COVARIATEGROUPS
#> 1 85.4  47   1      1      0      0       Reference

# Matrix reference: same shape as dfCovs, active cells set to the reference,
# inactive cells keep missVal
setupDfRefRow(dfCovs,
  data = dfData, covariates = covs, singleRef = FALSE,
  idVar = "ID"
)
#>       WT AGE SEX GENO_2 GENO_3 GENO_4 COVARIATEGROUPS
#> 1   85.4 -99 -99    -99    -99    -99              WT
#> 2   85.4 -99 -99    -99    -99    -99              WT
#> 3  -99.0  47 -99    -99    -99    -99             AGE
#> 4  -99.0  47 -99    -99    -99    -99             AGE
#> 5  -99.0 -99   1    -99    -99    -99             SEX
#> 6  -99.0 -99   1    -99    -99    -99             SEX
#> 7  -99.0 -99 -99      1      0      0            GENO
#> 8  -99.0 -99 -99      1      0      0            GENO
#> 9  -99.0 -99 -99      1      0      0            GENO
#> 10 -99.0 -99 -99      1      0      0            GENO

# Pin WT at the model's normalisation weight and take AGE from the mean
setupDfRefRow(dfCovs,
  data = dfData, covariates = covs, idVar = "ID",
  contRef = list(WT = 75, default = "mean")
)
#>   WT  AGE SEX GENO_2 GENO_3 GENO_4 COVARIATEGROUPS
#> 1 75 45.9   1      1      0      0       Reference

# Take every reference from the control stream, so the reference row agrees
# with a parameter function generated from the same model
modFile <- system.file("extdata", "SimVal/run7.mod", package = "PMXForest")
covs2 <- c("WT", "SEX", "FOOD", "FORM")
dfCovs2 <- setupDfCovs(dfData, covariates = covs2, idVar = "ID")
setupDfRefRow(dfCovs2,
  data = dfData, covariates = covs2, idVar = "ID",
  contRef = "model", catRef = "model", model = modFile
)
#>   WT SEX FOOD FORM COVARIATEGROUPS
#> 1 75   1    1    1       Reference
